name: Transfeminism
summary: Transfeminism is a strand of feminism built by trans women, who hold that their liberation is bound up with the liberation of all women. It defends each person's right to define their identity and decide about their body, resists medical and moral gatekeeping and the binary gender system, and, in its intersectional form, treats sexism, racism and class as overlapping. Its documented positions are mostly about gender, bodies, violence, sexuality and the inclusion of trans women; its sources say little on economics, government or world affairs.
scope: Transfeminism as stated in Emi Koyama's Transfeminist Manifesto (2000-2001) and essays, Julia Serano's writings on trans feminism, Sandy Stone's Posttranssexual Manifesto, and the abolitionist radical transfeminism of Nat Raha and Mijke van der Drift. It excludes feminism, queer politics and the left in general, and gender-critical feminism that disputes trans women's inclusion; answers are given only where these texts settle a statement.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Manifesto says transfeminists should join reproductive choice organisations and demonstrate for choice, and ties trans women's cause to women's right to decide about pregnancy; Koyama's campus essay defends abortion as a constitutionally protected right.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Manifesto describes violence against women as a systematic function of the patriarchy that keeps all women subjugated, speaks of male supremacy and the heterosexist patriarchy, and Serano's account of sexism likewise starts from men being treated as more legitimate than women.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Koyama's postscript concedes that any feminist theory that fails to account for racism, classism and ableism among women is incomplete, and Serano calls transfeminism intersectional because sexism, racism and classism act on and exacerbate each other.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Manifesto holds that nobody should be coerced into or out of gender roles and confronts institutions that narrow women's choices, so a law prescribing distinct roles for men and women is what transfeminism is organised against.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The first principle of the Manifesto is that each person has the right to define their own identity and to expect society to respect it and to express gender without discrimination or violence; it also demands action against employment and service discrimination against trans people.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The Manifesto states that transfeminism holds sex and gender are both socially constructed and treats the sex/gender split as artificial (the section on reverse essentialism); Serano, the other main voice, qualifies this with a role for biology, so the founding text is the stated position.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Koyama's Manifesto treats gender as constructed, but Serano accepts social construction only as one part of a holistic account in which biology and its variation also shape gender and rejects gender being 'just a construct', so the two main strands differ on 'primarily'.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Koyama argues that there are as many ways of being a woman as there are women, that a single universal female experience is a fallacy, and that a feminism drawing a clear boundary around 'women' is wrong; Serano calls the universal women's experience a myth debunked by women of colour.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Koyama's pamphlet for the prostitutes' rights movement treats sex work as labour, says anti-prostitution laws are used by police and pimps to harass workers, and calls anti-prostitution activists' collusion with law enforcement oppressive.

premarital-sex.rationale: Koyama holds that everyone is entitled to their own definition of sexuality and that a dominant group enforcing its sexual ideology on others is sexual oppression; Serano's account of sexism similarly treats sex-shaming of women as a double standard.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Transfeminism is framed as an alliance with queers and lesbians against homophobia and the persecution of sexual minorities, so punishing same-sex relations is the kind of oppression its sources oppose.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Manifesto says no political, medical or religious authority may override a person's decisions about their body and that nobody should be coerced in how they express gender, which a legal duty on women to cover contradicts.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Manifesto opposes forced and coerced sterilisation and says no authority may violate bodily integrity against a person's will; it also calls surgery imposed on intersex children abusive.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Koyama endorses harm reduction, which meets drug users where they are without coercion and opposes criminalising and punishing drug use, and the Manifesto denounces authorities' indifference to murders of marginalised women; state killing of drug users contradicts both.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Manifesto treats discrimination in employment and services as a central harm to trans women and calls for shelters and agencies to serve them, so a right of private owners to refuse anyone on any grounds contradicts its demands.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Raha and van der Drift present transfeminism as abolition (their book's subtitle and publisher summary), and Koyama's shelter essay, quoting Angela Davis, questions reliance on a racist state and criminalisation to end violence against women; no strand argues for keeping police and prisons.

material-over-identity.rationale: Koyama's postscript insists feminism be multi-issue and attend to class and race together with gender, and the whole transfeminist project asks for recognition of trans identity, so confining the left to workers' material interests runs against it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Koyama rejects pressure to conform and purity tests in either direction, but Serano criticises subversivism, the praise of unconventional genders simply for being unconventional, so the encouragement of eccentricity is split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Koyama warns that saying women or men have identifiably different minds can justify discrimination, while Serano argues for empowering femininity; neither says women bring distinct public values that deserve more weight.

notes: Searched theme by theme: Koyama's Manifesto, her readings (sex work, harm reduction, shelters, race, abortion) and FAQ; Serano's website, blog and the Ms. essay; Stone; the Raha/van der Drift publisher text and Raha's abstract. The texts are rich on gender, bodies, medicine, violence, sexuality, intersectionality and trans inclusion, and nearly silent on economics, government, world affairs, technology and ecology, so those stay null. Koyama's own postscript says the Manifesto is narrow and focused on trans women. The old audit's economic, institutional and foreign-policy answers rested on the 'left outlook' and are dropped. Strands: Koyama treats sex and gender as constructed, Serano holds a holistic view with biology; Raha and van der Drift (abolitionist, anti-capitalist) go beyond the earlier mainstream. Raha's and van der Drift's book text, Serano's Whipping Girl and Excluded full text, Serano's Medium essays, Bettcher's Philosophy Compass article, Spade's and Feinberg's writings were not used (see report); Feinberg and Spade were left out as trans liberation rather than transfeminism.
